turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: I must say, Mr. Worthing, that your address is rather out of the ordinary range. One might almost think that you are trying to avoid the notice of the social world.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Mamma, surely Mr. Worthing's address is of no consequence. I am engaged to him, and that is all there is to it.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Gwendolen, the carriage! Mr. Worthing, I am afraid I must insist on a more satisfactory explanation of your circumstances. Your address is not the sort of thing that should be left to the imagination.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Mamma, you are being unreasonable. I love Mr. Worthing, and that is enough.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Gwendolen, I have told you repeatedly that love is not a sufficient basis for a marriage. Mr. Worthing, it seems to me that you are evading the truth. You must provide me with a satisfactory explanation of your background and your address.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: I understand, Lady Bracknell. I am willing to provide any information you require to the best of my ability.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: I am not interested in your vague assurances, Mr. Worthing. I require facts. Now, I must insist that you provide me with a clear and satisfactory explanation of your background and address immediately.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Lady Bracknell, I assure you that I will do my utmost to provide you with all the information you need. My background and the details of my address are indeed important, and I am prepared to explain them fully.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Mr. Worthing, your assurances are not enough. You must provide me with concrete details. I have no patience for vagueness.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: I understand your concerns, Lady Bracknell. I will do my best to provide the information you seek in a clear and detailed manner.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Mr. Worthing, I require precise and truthful answers. Begin by telling me about your parents and your place of birth.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Lady Bracknell, I was unfortunately orphaned at a very early age and was brought up by a series of guardians. My place of birth is London, though my residence is now in the countryside.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Mr. Worthing, your unfortunate orphanhood is of course regrettable, but it does not diminish the necessity for you to provide me with the names and social standing of your guardians. And your place of birth, London, is rather vague. Could you be more specific about your circumstances?

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: I apologize, Lady Bracknell. My guardians were a series of respectable gentlemen and ladies, but I cannot recall their exact names or social standing. As for my birth, I was born near the Marble Arch in London, but I have no specific address or details to provide.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Mr. Worthing, the vagueness of your background is rather troubling. I must insist on more concrete details. Can you provide any specific addresses or connections that might shed light on your origins?

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: I am afraid, Lady Bracknell, that I cannot provide more specific details. My early life was indeed rather uncertain, and I have no documents or addresses to offer.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Mr. Worthing, your inability to provide any concrete information about your background is most unsatisfactory. I must remind you that I am not accustomed to such vagueness in matters of marriage.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: I understand your concerns, Lady Bracknell. I wish I could provide you with more details, but my early years were indeed shrouded in uncertainty.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: I see, Mr. Worthing. Your lack of clarity is indeed disappointing. I must now consider your proposal with the utmost seriousness. Gwendolen, the carriage!

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: I am sorry to have disappointed you, Lady Bracknell. I assure you, I have always tried to be honest about the facts I know.

opening.speaker: Gwendolen
opening.text: I am engaged to Mr. Worthing, mamma.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Pardon me, you are not engaged to any one. When you do become engaged to some one, I, or your father, will inform you of the fact. An engagement should come on a young girl as a surprise, pleasant or unpleasant, as the case may be. It is hardly a matter that she could be allowed to arrange for herself . . . And now I have a few questions to put to you, Mr. Worthing. While I am making these inquiries, you, Gwendolen, will wait for me below in the carriage.

opening.speaker: Gwendolen
opening.text: Mamma!

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: In the carriage, Gwendolen!

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Gwendolen, the carriage!

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: You can take a seat, Mr. Worthing.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Thank you, Lady Bracknell, I prefer standing.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: I feel bound to tell you that you are not down on my list of eligible young men, although I have the same list as the dear Duchess of Bolton has. We work together, in fact. However, I am quite ready to enter your name, should your answers be what a really affectionate mother requires. Do you smoke?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Well, yes, I must admit I smoke.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: I am glad to hear it. A man should always have an occupation of some kind. There are far too many idle men in London as it is. How old are you?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Twenty-nine.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: A very good age to be married at. I have always been of opinion that a man who desires to get married should know either everything or nothing. Which do you know?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: I know nothing, Lady Bracknell.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: I am pleased to hear it. I do not approve of anything that tampers with natural ignorance. Ignorance is like a delicate exotic fruit; touch it and the bloom is gone. The whole theory of modern education is radically unsound. Fortunately in England, at any rate, education produces no effect whatsoever. If it did, it would prove a serious danger to the upper classes, and probably lead to acts of violence in Grosvenor Square. What is your income?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Between seven and eight thousand a year.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: In land, or in investments?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: In investments, chiefly.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: That is satisfactory. What between the duties expected of one during one’s lifetime, and the duties exacted from one after one’s death, land has ceased to be either a profit or a pleasure. It gives one position, and prevents one from keeping it up. That’s all that can be said about land.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: I have a country house with some land, of course, attached to it, about fifteen hundred acres, I believe; but I dons depend on that for my real income. In fact, as far as I can make out, the poachers are the only people who make anything out of it.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: A country house! How many bedrooms? Well, that point can be cleared up afterwards. You have a town house, I hope? A girl with a simple, unspoiled nature, like Gwendolen, could hardly be expected to reside in the country.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Well, I own a house in Belgrave Square, but it is let by the year to Lady Bloxham. Of course, I can get it back whenever I like, at six months’ notice.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bloxham? I don’t know her.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Oh, she goes about very little. She is a lady considerably advanced in years.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Ah, nowadays that is no guarantee of respectability of character. What number in Belgrave Square?
